cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. David is king of Israel, and this story opens with trouble. Satan rises up against Israel and stirs David up to do something.

cards.question: Satan stirs up King David to do what?

cards.text: So David tells Joab, the commander of his army (1 Chronicles 18:15), and the troop commanders to go count the Israelites from Beersheba to Dan and bring him the number. And I bet Joab feels the dread you get when the boss says, "Quick favor," and you KNOW it isn't.

cards.question: Joab hears David's order to count the Israelites. What does he say back to the king?

answers.text: He asks why David would bring guilt on Israel
He says the troops are too worn out to travel
He asks David to wait until after the harvest

cards.question: Joab's pushback works, and King David calls off the count.

cards.text: The king's word wins, so Joab travels all over Israel and reports back: 1,100,000 men who drew the sword, 470,000 of them in Judah. I used to count falling dust in a junk drawer for fun, and even I'd need a NAP after that number.

cards.question: Joab's count leaves out two tribes: Benjamin and ___.
Joab leaves two tribes out of the count because King David's command is detestable to him.

cards.text: Turns out Joab isn't alone on this one. The command is evil in the sight of God too, and He strikes Israel.

cards.question: After God strikes Israel, King David blames Joab for doing the counting.

cards.text: David tells God, "I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing." No "well, TECHNICALLY Joab did the counting," just a king begging God to take away his iniquity.
Then the LORD instructs Gad, David's seer.

cards.question: Through Gad the seer, what does the LORD offer King David?

answers.text: A way to undo the census
Forty days to make it right

cards.text: Here's the list: three years of famine, three months swept away before his enemies, or three days of the sword of the LORD, a plague with the angel of the LORD ravaging every part of Israel. Then Gad asks David what answer to take back to the One who sent him.

cards.question: King David has to pick one of the three. What does he choose?

answers.text: To fall into the hand of the LORD
To fall into the hands of his enemies
To face three years of famine

cards.question: David would rather fall into the LORD's hand than the hands of men, because the LORD's ___ are very great.

cards.text: So the LORD sends a plague on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fall dead. That's a heavy one, friend.
Then God sends an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But as the angel is doing it, the LORD sees it.

cards.question: When the LORD sees the angel destroying Jerusalem, He lets the angel keep going.

cards.text: The LORD relents and tells the angel, "Enough! Withdraw your hand now!" Right then, the angel of the LORD is standing by a threshing floor that belongs to a Jebusite.
David looks up and sees the angel of the LORD standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem.

cards.question: King David and the elders see the angel with the drawn sword over Jerusalem. What do they do?

answers.text: Run to hide inside the city walls
Send for the priests to bring the ark

cards.text: Then David speaks to God. He says he's the one who gave the order to count the people, and then he asks, "But these sheep, what have they done?"

cards.question: David asks God to let His hand fall on David and his father's house, and not let the plague stay on the people.

cards.text: Then the angel of the LORD orders Gad to bring David a message: go up and build an altar to the LORD.

cards.question: David is told to build the altar on the threshing floor of ___ the Jebusite.

cards.text: So David goes up, just like Gad said. Meanwhile Ornan is threshing wheat, and he turns and sees the angel.

cards.question: Ornan's four sons are with him when he turns and sees the angel. What do the sons do?

answers.text: They run to tell the king
They bow down to the angel

cards.text: Then David arrives, and Ornan bows facedown before him. David asks to buy the threshing floor for the full price, so he can build the altar and the plague can be halted.

cards.question: King David wants to buy Ornan's threshing floor. What does Ornan say?

answers.text: He offers to give David all of it
He asks for twice the full price
He says the land isn't his to sell

cards.question: Ornan even throws in the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood and the wheat for the grain offering. David turns it all down and insists on paying the full price. Why?

answers.text: He won't give offerings that cost him nothing
He thinks Ornan's oxen are too old to offer
He wants the priests to bring the wood

cards.text: So David pays Ornan six hundred shekels of gold for the site. Then he builds an altar there, offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, and calls on the LORD.

cards.question: David calls on the LORD at the new altar, and the LORD answers him with ___ from heaven on the altar.
Then the LORD speaks to the angel, and the angel puts his sword back into its sheath.

cards.text: When David sees the LORD has answered him, he offers sacrifices right there. The tabernacle that Moses, Israel's leader, made in the wilderness is at the high place in Gibeon, but David can't go there to inquire of God, because he's afraid of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

cards.question: Then King David speaks about Ornan's threshing floor. What does he say?

answers.text: Here will be the house of the LORD God
Here will be the palace of the king
Here will be a city for the Levites
